verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI's first-party durable-execution docs say agents can preserve progress across failures, application errors or restarts. They also say it handles long-running, asynchronous and human-in-the-loop workflows, and the homepage cites running agents on a durable background queue. Missing for 10: explicit coverage of surviving deploys, named durable-execution integrations and how they work, and independent or hands-on corroboration of restart durability.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run long-lived agents durably across process restarts and deploys, natively or via durable-execution integrations

citations.quote: Pydantic AI allows you to build durable agents that can preserve their progress across transient API failures and application errors or restarts, and handle long-running, asynchronous, and human-in-the-loop workflows with production-grade reliability.
The same agent runs everywhere you need it: behind a web frontend, in the terminal, on a voice call, on a durable background queue, or as a plain object you call run() on.
